title: Why Man Needs Morality
summary: Why a code of values is a requirement of human life, not a decoration.

lessons.title: A code of values
lessons.objective: Name morality as a code of values that guides choices and actions, not a mood or a slogan.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what is morality?

choices.text: A code of values that guides choices and actions
A mood that comes and goes
A decoration added after life is already secure
A list of other people's tastes

feedback.note: Morality here means a code of values used to guide what you choose and what you do.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the role this unit gives it.

pairs.right: A guide for choices and actions

feedback.note: A mood is not yet a code. A code is a guide you can apply to choices and actions.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit's name for morality.

feedback.note: The two words to hold are code and values. Decoration and whim are the contrasts, not the definition.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that says what a code of values does.

feedback.note: The code's job is to guide choices. It does not decorate moods.

exercises.prompt: Which question does a code of values answer?

choices.text: What should I choose, and how should I act?
How should I feel once the action is over?
How should a finished life look from outside?
Which choices can I skip because I am already alive?

feedback.note: A code is for choosing and acting. It is not a report of feelings after the fact, and it is not a look.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to what it is in this lesson.

pairs.right: A standard you can apply again
A phrase that does not guide action

feedback.note: A code can be used on the next choice. A whim and a slogan cannot do that work.

exercises.prompt: Say what the code guides.

feedback.note: Choices and actions are what the code is for. Ornaments and slogans are not substitutes.

exercises.prompt: Build the definition you are learning.

feedback.note: Morality is a code of values. Luxury and hobby drop the idea of a guide for action.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is not a code of values?

choices.text: Today's passing mood
A standard for choosing actions
A guide you can use more than once
A set of values held as a code

feedback.note: A passing mood is not a code. A code is a standard you can use again when you choose.

exercises.prompt: Why call it a code rather than a single value?

choices.text: It has to guide many choices, not one isolated wish
A person is allowed only one action in a life
A longer list looks more decorative
Values are unnecessary if the list is long

feedback.note: A code covers the choices and actions of a life. One isolated wish is not that guide.

lessons.title: Why human life requires it
lessons.objective: Explain why a being who must choose needs a code of values, while a life of automatic action does not.

exercises.prompt: Why does a human being need a code of values?

choices.text: He must choose the actions his life requires
Other species vote on his values
Decoration is the purpose of ethics
Human life continues with no choices at all

feedback.note: The need comes from having to choose the actions on which a human life depends.

exercises.prompt: Match each kind of life to how values are pursued.

pairs.right: Pursues values by its nature, automatically
Must choose, and so needs a code

feedback.note: Automatic action does not need a chosen code. Chosen action does.

exercises.prompt: Complete the reason a person needs a code.

feedback.note: Life requires certain actions, and a person has to choose them. That is why a code is required.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim about human life.

feedback.note: Human life requires a code of values. Optional is the word this unit rejects.

exercises.prompt: What is different about human action in this unit?

choices.text: The values a human life needs are not pursued automatically
Instinct never fails, so no code is needed
Values are decorations added at the end
Being alive already settles every choice

feedback.note: A human life is not programmed the way an animal's pursuit of values is. The actions have to be chosen.

exercises.prompt: Match each fact to the conclusion this lesson draws.

feedback.note: Take away the code and the choices a human life depends on have no guide.

exercises.prompt: Contrast the two kinds of life.

parts.text: An animal does not need a conceptual
. A person does, because action is

feedback.note: The conceptual code is needed because human action is chosen, not because decoration demands it.

exercises.prompt: Build the short link between choice and a code.

feedback.note: Once action is chosen, it needs a code. Whim and instinct are not that code.

exercises.prompt: If action is chosen, what supplies the guide?

choices.text: A code of values
The fact that other species act automatically
A decoration
The absence of any standard

feedback.note: Other species do not need the code you need. Absence of a standard does not guide a choice.

exercises.prompt: Name what chosen action has to sustain.

parts.text: The code is required so chosen action can sustain a human

feedback.note: The thing to be sustained is a human life. An ornament, a mood, or a slogan is not the reason for the code.

lessons.title: Not a decoration
lessons.objective: Reject the idea that morality is an optional ornament, a luxury, or something added only after life is secure.

exercises.prompt: On this unit's account, a code of values is what?

choices.text: A requirement of human life
A decoration you may skip
Useful only on special occasions
A costume for people who already know how to live

feedback.note: The unit's word is requirement. Decoration, occasion, and costume all treat the code as optional.

exercises.prompt: Match each label to the status it gives morality.

pairs.right: The same mistake as calling it a decoration

feedback.note: Optional extra is another way of saying decoration. This unit says the code is a requirement.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit summary.

parts.text: A code of values is a

feedback.note: Requirement of human life is the claim. Luxury and ornament are the errors being set aside.

exercises.prompt: Build the contrast in the unit title's idea.

feedback.note: The code is not a decoration of human life. Calling it a luxury says the same false thing.

exercises.prompt: When is the code needed?

choices.text: In order to live, not after living is finished
Only after every practical need is already met
Only when you want to look moral
Never, if you are already alive

feedback.note: The code is a means of living. Waiting until life is finished treats morality as trim.

exercises.prompt: Match each aim to requirement or decoration.

pairs.left: Skip the code and still expect a policy

feedback.note: Choosing how to live is the requirement. Looking moral, or skipping the code, is the decorative mistake.

exercises.prompt: Say what morality is not.

parts.text: you add when life is already

feedback.note: An ornament added once life is secure is the view this unit denies. The code is required in order to live.

exercises.prompt: Build the status of the code.

feedback.note: The code is a requirement. Luxury and trim are the names to leave out.

exercises.prompt: Which line matches the unit?

choices.text: A code of values is required by human life
Morality is the frosting on survival
Live first and adopt a code later
Values are a hobby for quiet weekends

feedback.note: Frosting, later, and hobby all make the code a decoration. The unit says human life requires it.

lessons.title: Without a code
lessons.objective: See that without a code, choices have no standard, so action drifts by whim and is not a policy for living.

exercises.prompt: Without a code of values, what guides a choice?

choices.text: Whim, the feeling of the moment
A standard you can apply tomorrow
A stated requirement of human life
A code you refused to name but still use

feedback.note: Drop the code and what is left is the feeling of the moment. That feeling is not a standard for tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Match each way of acting to what it is.

pairs.right: Action with no policy for living

feedback.note: A code holds from choice to choice. Whim and drift do not make a policy for living.

exercises.prompt: Name the contrast.

parts.text: A feeling of the moment is a

feedback.note: Whim is not a code. A policy and a requirement belong with the code, not with the moment's feeling.

exercises.prompt: Build the rejection of whim.

feedback.note: Whim is not a code of values. A policy would be a code you can keep using.

exercises.prompt: Why can't whim do the job of a code?

choices.text: It does not give a standard you can use from choice to choice
It is the same thing as a code of values
It automatically serves human life
It is a decoration, and decorations are requirements

feedback.note: A code has to reach the next choice. A whim expires with the moment and does not serve life by default.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to whether it can guide a life.

feedback.note: Swapping moods does not create a code. A code is the guide that stays in force.

exercises.prompt: Say what a policy needs.

parts.text: To live by a policy, you need a

feedback.note: A policy lasts beyond one moment, so it has to be a code. Whim and ornament do not last as guides.

exercises.prompt: Build the reach of a code.

feedback.note: A code reaches past the moment. A whim does not.

exercises.prompt: Range-of-the-moment action is which of these?

choices.text: Not yet a morality
The definition of a code of values
How plants choose a code
The decoration that human life requires

feedback.note: Action that only tracks the moment is not a morality. Morality is a code, and human life requires that code, not a decoration.

exercises.prompt: What is this lesson's contrast?

choices.text: A code of values versus whim
Decoration versus ornament
Animal life versus plant life
One slogan versus another slogan

feedback.note: The contrast is code versus whim. Decoration and ornament are the same mistake, and plants are not choosing codes.

lessons.title: The reason, held together
lessons.objective: State the full claim: man needs morality because a code of values is required to choose the actions human life depends on, and that need is not decorative.

exercises.prompt: Why does man need morality, on this unit's account?

choices.text: A code of values is a requirement of human life
A code of values is a decoration of human life
Animals need the same conceptual code
Whim already is a code

feedback.note: Man needs morality because human life requires a code of values. Animals do not need that conceptual code, and whim is not one.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the unit to its place.

pairs.right: Not a substitute for the code

feedback.note: Hold four pieces: the person who needs the code, what the code guides, the status of the need, and the substitute that fails.

exercises.prompt: State why man needs morality.

parts.text: Man needs morality because human life

feedback.note: Human life requires a code of values. It does not decorate whims.

exercises.prompt: Build the unit summary's main clause.

feedback.note: A code of values is a requirement of human life. Decoration is the word the summary refuses.

exercises.prompt: Which set is the whole claim?

choices.text: A code of values, required by human life, not a decoration
Decoration, whim, and automatic instinct
Mood, slogan, and luxury
Plant life, animal life, and no choices

feedback.note: The whole claim has three parts: code of values, required by human life, and not a decoration.

exercises.prompt: Match each status to the life it belongs to.

pairs.right: A life that must choose its actions
A life that pursues values automatically
The status of the code for a human being

feedback.note: The requirement attaches to a life of chosen action. For that life, the code is not a decoration.

exercises.prompt: Say what the code is for.

feedback.note: Chosen action in the service of life is the work of the code. Ornament and display are not.

exercises.prompt: Build what morality does for the choices life depends on.

feedback.note: Morality guides the choices life depends on. It does not decorate a whim.

exercises.prompt: Which mistake drops the point of the unit?

choices.text: Treating the code as an optional ornament
Treating the code as a requirement
Treating whim as not enough
Treating human life as the reason for the code

feedback.note: The mistake is to treat the code as an optional ornament. Requirement, the failure of whim, and human life as the reason are the unit itself.

exercises.prompt: Build the short form of the title's answer.

feedback.note: Man needs morality to live. Decorate and display are the uses this unit rules out.
